core_meaning.primary_meaning: Umar (Arabic عمر, ʿUmar), also written Omar, is an Arabic male name meaning “flourishing” or “long-lived”. Among Muslims it chiefly honours Umar ibn al-Khattab, companion of the Prophet Muhammad and the second Rashidun caliph, known by the title al-Fārūq, “the Distinguisher”.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The name is linked to the Arabic root ʿ-m-r, associated with life and lifespan (ʿumr, “life”) and with flourishing, inhabited land.

etymology.morphology: Personal name of the fuʿal pattern from ʿ-m-r.
etymology.etymology_explanation: From the Arabic root ع م ر, “to live long; to flourish”.
etymology.false_etymology_warning: Hebrew omer (“sheaf”) and Germanic Ómar/Ottomar are unrelated names that happen to look alike.

origin.origin_explanation: Arabic; spread through the Muslim world. The Turkish form is Ömer and the Bosnian Omer.

religion.religious_status: Name of the second Rashidun caliph
religion.religious_explanation: Umar ibn al-Khattab (c. 584–644) at first opposed Muhammad, converted to Islam in 616 and became the first Muslim to pray openly at the Kaaba. Muhammad gave him the title al-Fārūq, “the Distinguisher”. He succeeded Abu Bakr as caliph in 634 and ruled until his assassination in 644; he was also the father of Hafsa, a wife of the Prophet.

prophetic_status.reference: Umar ibn al-Khattab, companion and father-in-law of the Prophet

cultural_context.cultural_meaning: In Sunni tradition Umar is a model of justice and firm judgement — the sense of his title al-Fārūq.

pronunciation.note: Often said OH-mar in English; Turkish Ömer.

name_variants.variant_notes: Omar (English/Spanish), Ömer (Turkish), Omer (Bosnian), Oumar (West Africa), Umer (South Asia).

known_linguistic_history: Umar I ruled as caliph 634–644 and drove much of the early Muslim conquests.
Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (Umar II) was Umayyad caliph 717–720.
historical_context.historical_person_association: Umar ibn al-Khattab (c. 584–644), second Rashidun caliph.

modern_usage.modern_context: Common across the Muslim world; Omar is the usual English and Spanish spelling.

faq.a: “Flourishing” or “long-lived”, from the Arabic root ʿ-m-r.
The second Rashidun caliph (r. 634–644), a senior companion and father-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad.
“The Distinguisher” — the title Muhammad gave Umar for his sound judgement.

faq.q: Is Umar the same as Omar?
faq.a: Yes, both transliterate عمر. Ömer is the Turkish form.
No. Hebrew omer means “sheaf” and is a separate word.

islamic_naming_context.context: Given in honour of Umar ibn al-Khattab; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (Umar II), the Umayyad caliph, is another celebrated bearer.
islamic_naming_context.interpretation: Chosen for the companion's example of justice and for the meaning “long-lived”.
islamic_naming_context.important_distinction: Lexical meaning and the honour of the companion are separate reasons for the name.

numerology.meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Umar total 8, associated with ambition, authority and material success. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.
numerology.note: Numerology is an optional interpretive layer, not a linguistic fact.
